tasks.title: Dispose the MatchSim in DirectFireWithoutTankGunneryRefusesToStep
tasks.why: P2, CombatTests.cs:373. The new test builds the sim with a plain `var m = MatchSim.CreateGreybox(cfg, combat: false);` -- no `using`, and nothing else in the method disposes it. The test's whole point is that the next Step throws (CombatTests.cs:376), so even a trailing Dispose would be skipped. Every MatchSim holds Allocator.Persistent NativeArrays (SimWorld.cs:156-181), so each run of this test leaks a whole world and Unity reports "A Native Collection has not been disposed" later, against whatever test or domain reload happens to trip it -- a red the gate blames on an innocent test. It is the only `CreateGreybox(cfg, combat: false)` in the tests without `using` (the other seven at LockstepLoopbackTests.cs:45, LaneAndEngageRulesTests.cs:225, SpreadAndEngageTests.cs:277,307 all have it).
tasks.done_when: the test reads `using var m = ...` (or wraps the throw in try/finally with m.Dispose()), the EditMode run of CombatTests is green, and its log holds no "Native Collection has not been disposed" line

tasks.title: Probe SimWorld.Roster in the tick-hash blind-spot test
tasks.why: P2, BattlefieldLockstepTests.cs:287-298. The probe list says it is "every array SimWorld.Hash() folds in, in the order it folds them", but Hash() folds Roster (SimWorld.cs:448, `SimHash.Array(Roster, h)`) between AliveCount and Silver and no probe touches it. Roster is the per-player deploy table (SimWorld.cs:50, MaxPlayers * RosterEntry.SlotCount, written by FillRosters at :112-134), the seam's own RosterEntry.SlotCount surface: if it were dropped from Hash() two peers could deploy different units from the same slot and every lockstep test in the repo would stay green. This is exactly the gap [T24b] just closed for Alarm, left open one array earlier in the same fold.
tasks.done_when: a Roster probe (NativeArray<RosterEntry>, perturb element 0 and put it back) sits in the list where Hash() folds it, the test is green, and it goes red when the `SimHash.Array(Roster, h)` line in SimWorld.Hash() is commented out

tasks.title: Fix the five wrong line citations in the new lockstep comments
tasks.why: P3, BattlefieldLockstepTests.cs:100-102, :150-151, :298, :329 and BreakerTests.cs:166. The [T9]/[T24b] rewrite justifies itself by citing lines, and four of its five citations point at unrelated code: "Tick is folded into World.Hash() (SimWorld.cs:392)" -- 392 is inside ClampToMap, Tick is folded at :440; "it folds Silver in (SimWorld.cs:163, :402)" -- 163 allocates Layer and 402 is a Phase0MoveJob field, Silver is folded at :449; "LastHash ... (SimWorld.cs:247-253 / :240-253 only writes it on a tick it hashes)" -- that range is Spawn/Despawn, LastHash is written at :289 and :292; "Alarm, folded at SimWorld.cs:439 since v27" -- 439 is `SimHash.Value(Tick, h)`, Alarm is at :477. BreakerTests.cs:166's "the halt the wind-up asks for (Breaker.cs:99)" is the Phase assignment; the halt is Breaker.cs:101. Every claim is true; only the pointers are wrong, so the next reader who checks the reasoning at the line (the review rule) finds unrelated code and cannot tell a stale comment from a wrong one. MatchSim.cs:76 and Replay.cs:17 both read true.
tasks.done_when: each cited SimWorld.cs/Breaker.cs line number names the statement the comment describes, checked by reading the file at that line; no test behaviour changes and the EditMode modules for these two files stay green
